The roof is relatively flat with a ¼-inch per foot slope and maximum height of 57’ that is used consistently at the 4 corners reported (Points 1-4).  Atop the roof are two exhaust stacks that are 19’ and 26’ higher than maximum roof height.  Using the higher of the two stacks  the “Total Structure Height” reported for Points 1-4 is 83’ (57+26).  Attachments 2  3  and 4 provide the coordinates of the footprint  perspective of the building and roof stacks  and cross-sections respectively.nThe building’s roof will be topped with a PVC membrane.

The building’s location is currently occupied by office trailers and storage containers and compactors for Boeing’s material recycling. nRelative to Charleston International Airport  the building will be 3 900-feet (0.74-miles) southeast of the threshold of Runway 03 and 4 000 feet (0.76-miles) south of the threshold of Runway 33.  The building is also 3 000-feet (0.57-miles) west of Interstate 526.  Attachment 1 illustrates the location.nnIt should be noted that the location is deemed "On Airport" since the property is leased to Boeing by an affiliate of Charleston International Airport.

STRUCTURE NAME: Boeing South Carolina - FGI Stalls T1-T4
PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: Boeing South Carolina proposes to construct a concrete apron as part of its ongoing aerospace campus expansion in North Charleston South Carolina and adjacent to Charleston International Airport (CHS).  The apron will accommodate four airplane parking positions  referred to as T1  T2  T3  and T4.nnThe new apron will have a footprint of approximately 380 000 square feet (8.7 acres) with perimeter dimensions of 433’ x 875’.  The apron is relatively flat with an elevation range from 15 to 18 and slopes less than one percent (1%).  Its southerly limit will match the existing elevations of Taxiway ‘M’.nnThe apron will predominately accommodate the 787 Dreamliner aircraft with the 787-10 having the highest tail height of 55.8 feet.  Also  the T-1 stall could potentially receive Boeing’s Dreamlifter that is a 747-400LCF with a tail height of 70.7 feet.  The Dreamlifter’s tail location and height is applied on the application’s AGL input.  It is noted that behind the tail of the plane positions  the proposed improvements will include three (3) temporary trailers  each of which being approximately 25 feet by 60 feet.  With these trailers being less than 20 feet tall  they will be below the lowest tail height of adjacent aircraft.nnIt is also noted that light poles will be part of the project and submitted as a separate determination request.nAttachment 2 provides the coordinates of the footprint and tail heights.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: Boeing South Carolina proposes to construct a concrete apron as part of its ongoing aerospace campus expansion in North Charleston South Carolina and adjacent to Charleston International Airport (CHS). The apron’s location is currently undeveloped. nRelative to Charleston International Airport  the closest corner of the apron will be 3 300 feet (0.63-miles) south of the threshold of Runway 33 and 4 500 feet (0.85-miles) east of the threshold of Runway 03. The Project will provide the Airport’s passenger facility  navigational aids  and personnel with a resilient  continuous electric service to operate safely and efficiently.

A Final Determination for the building itself was issued via ASN 2024-ASO-15457-NRA.  nnConstruction of the FAB will require use of cranes up to 395' high.  A crane box has been established for this submittal with the location and elevation of the four (4) perimeter corners being consistent with the included Class 1A survey.nRelative to Charleston International Airport (CHS)  the closest edges of the crane box will be 5 000 feet (0.95-miles) southeast of the threshold of Runway 03 and 5 900 feet (1.12 miles) south of the threshold of Runway 33.  The crane box is also 1 200 feet (0.23 miles) west of Interstate 526.nnIt should be noted that the location is deemed "On Airport" since the property is leased to Boeing by an affiliate of Charleston International Airport.nConstruction of the FAB will require use of cranes up to 395' high to erect the steel framing  150' man-lifts  and 150' high-lift fork-lifts to install the exterior cladding  roofing system  lighting  painting and misc. finishes all operating inside the crane box outlined below and in the attached 1A Survey.nnThe FAB building is approximately 600' wide and 1000' long with the center axis-oriented N-S.  The crane box is established 90 feet beyond / outside of the west  north and east sides and 210 feet beyond the south side.nnThe application entered the tallest crane height of 395 feet at each corner of the box  however  the variation in crane height and duration of use is further described as follows:nn-	Beginning January 1st  2026  through December 7th  2026  telehandlers operating at 225' AGL will be on site. Telehandlers can be lowered to the ground when not in usen-	Beginning April 1st  2026  through November 1st  2026  cranes operating at 325' AGL will be on site  resting height 285' AGLn-	Beginning April 25th  2026  through November 1st  2026  a crane operating at 395' AGL will be on site  resting height 367' AGLn-	Beginning February 17th  2026  through May 20th  2026  cranes operating at 255' AGL will be on site. Cranes can be lowered when not in use if necessary.n-	Beginning January 1  2026  through April 1  2027  various hydraulic cranes under 200’ will be utilized infrequently on the site to perform specific short term tasks throughout the timeframe.  These will be lowered and/or demobilized when not in use.

The objective of this project is to develop a grading and drainage strategy that brings the site to airfield-compatible elevations  manages stormwater runoff in compliance with regulatory requirements  and supports future infrastructure investments. The project will also establish a new access roadway connection to East Lake Boulevard. This proposal is for the geotechnical investigation across the project site to assess subsurface conditions and provide design parameters to support future development. To determine the subsurface conditions  the geotechnical firm proposes to perform 20 soil borings and multiple test pits distributed in a grid pattern.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The project was not required to file notice according to the FAA Pre-Screening Tool. However  the Kentucky Airport Zoning Commission (KAZC) requires that the solar project  given its location to Henderson City-County Airport  submit Form 7460-1 90 days prior to the proposed date of construction. The KAZC will use the aeronautical studies completed by the FAA on this project to guide their decision making for approval of a permit to construct the project near Henderson  KY. The project has an approved Construction Certificate from the State Siting Board and has been approved by the Henderson County Planning Commission. A previous Determination of No Hazard to Air Navigation was granted on 02/24/2021  but that approval is now expired.nnThe project includes approximately 418 acres of leased acreage. The panel height is 12 feet above ground level at maximum tilt. A ground-mounted solar photovoltaic system using single-axis trackers is planned to be used. Approximately 120 900 modules are expected. Each module will be mounted on a steel racking system supported by driven steel piles. Construction is planned to begin before the end of the year and is scheduled to be complete in January 2027. The project substation and gen-tie infrastructure will be submitted in a separate notice.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: Henderson County Solar is located approximately 3.5-miles Southwest of the City of Henderson. Highway 425 cuts through the middle of the project. Wilson Station Road borders the southernmost portion of the project to the south. US Hwy 41 A runs to the east of the project site. The project is approximately 2.5 miles Southwest of Henderson City-County Airport. Canoe Creek borders the norther part of the project to the north and to the east. Construction will involve installation of wood poles and stringing of conductors in accordance with industry standards and safety. However  the Kentucky Airport Zoning Commission (KAZC) requires that our utility poles  given their location to Henderson City-County Airport  submit Form 7460-1 90 days prior to the proposed date of construction. The KAZC will use the aeronautical studies completed by the FAA on this project to guide their decision making for approval of a permit to construct the project near Henderson  KY. The project has an approved Construction Certificate from the State Siting Board and has been approved by the Henderson County Planning Commission.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This submission is for a collector substation associated with a 50 MW utility-scale solar photovoltaic facility. The substation serves as the interconnection point between the project’s 69 kV generation tie-line (gen-tie) and the existing utility transmission system.nThe construction includes installation of steel support structures  transformers  circuit breakers  buswork  and associated electrical equipment. The tallest structure within the substation will be approximately 45 feet above ground level. The substation’s purpose is to step up the voltage from the solar generation output to the 69 kV transmission level  ensuring safe and efficient delivery of power to the utility grid.nThe substation is essential for integrating the solar project’s energy into the grid and maintaining system reliability.nAll other structures are submitted as separate notices.nThe project substation design is attached in Section 5.nnThe project was not required to file notice according to the FAA Pre-Screening Tool. However  the Kentucky Airport Zoning Commission (KAZC) requires that our solar project  given its location to Henderson City-County Airport  submit Form 7460-1 90 days prior to the proposed date of construction. The KAZC will use the aeronautical studies completed by the FAA on this project to guide their decision making for approval of a permit.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: Project Overview – ‘Welcome Home’ Housing DevelopmentnThe Welcome Home Housing Development is planned for the Park Hill Community in the City of Spartanburg  SC. The project includes:n•	Ten permanent rental housing units are distributed among five duplex buildings.n•	One non-congregate shelter located in a detached single-family house.n•	Supportive services available to residents on a voluntary basisnThe units are designated for individuals and families earning up to 30% or 60% of the Median Income Area (AMI). PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The equipment is a crawler crane (LR type) designed for heavy lifting operations. It is mounted on a tracked undercarriage  which provides stability and mobility across various terrain conditions. The crane will be configured with a main boom and an additional luffing jib (luffer) attachment to extend operational flexibility. The crawler undercarriage distributes ground pressure evenly  allowing safe movement and positioning on site. The main boom provides primary lifting capability and is engineered for heavy-duty performance  while the luffing jib enhances reach and versatility  enabling lifting operations at variable radii and angles. A modular counterweight system ensures stability during lifting operations  and the crane is intended for construction and industrial tasks requiring long reach and high capacity. This crane will be used for steel erection.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This project will upgrade existing sports lighting for the Church Street Park Cricket Field  located at 5817 Cricket Pitch Way  Morrisville  NC 27856. The six existing light poles received Determinations of No Hazard to Air Navigation under the following Aeronautical Study numbers:n2017-ASO-13794-OEn2017-ASO-13795-OEn2017-ASO-13796-OEn2017-ASO-13797-OEn2017-ASO-13798-OEn2017-ASO-13799-OEnnThe project may be completed in two phases but will most likely be completed as a single project. If phased  Phase 1 would upgrade the fixtures  wiring  and controls  and add additional fixtures on the existing Sports Light Poles. Phase 2 would add 4 additional 100’ light poles and the associated fixtures  controls and wiring like the existing light poles. In the  application we have listed them as 110’ to provide some buffer. nThe existing sports lighting consists of six 100’ tall concrete poles. These existing poles are denoted as P1-P6 on the provided plans. If Church Street is considered the 12:00 position  P1 is located at approximately 1:30  P2 at 10:30  P3 at 4:30  P4 at 7:30  P5 at 6:00  and P6 at 12:00. Each pole is topped by a lighting array that includes cross bars and individual light fixtures. Poles P1 and P3 are each topped with fourteen 1410-watt fixtures and two 575-watt ball-tracker fixtures at 15’ mounting heights. Poles P2 and P4 are each topped with nine 1410-watt fixtures  five 1170-watt fixtures  and two 575-watt ball-tracker fixtures at 15 to 20’ mounting heights. Poles P5 and P6 are each topped with thirteen 1410-watt fixtures  one 1170-watt fixtures  and two 575-watt ball-tracker fixtures at 15 to 20’ mounting heights. In total  there are seventy-two 1410-watt fixtures  twelve 1170-watt fixtures  and twelve 575-watt ball-tracker fixtures at 15 to 20’ mounting heights. nThis lighting system upgrade project has been designed with the possibility of being installed in two phases. The Town intends to pursue this as a single phase; however  funding and sports scheduling may require a two-phase approach. If a two-phased approach is used  Phase 1 will upgrade the pole tops on the six existing light poles. At the completion of Phase 1  there would be a total of ninety-five 1410-watt fixtures  twenty-five 1170-watt fixtures  and twelve 575-watt balltracker lights. Poles P1-P4 would each have twenty 1410-watt fixtures and two 575-watt ball-tracker fixtures. Pole P5 would have twelve 1170-watt fixtures  eight 1410-watt fixtures  and two 575-watt ball-tracker fixtures. Pole P6 would have thirteen 1170-watt fixtures  seven 1410-watt fixtures  and two 575-watt ball-tracker fixtures.  There will be no change in height for the existing poles. Phase 2 would take the project to the full lighting buildout.nAfter completion of Phase 2  the proposed plans will add four additional 100’ poles similar to the existing poles. If Church Street is considered the 12:00 position  E1 will be located at approximately 0:45  E2 at 11:15  W1 at 5:15  and W2 at 6:45. Poles E1  E2  W1  and W2 will each include twenty 1410-watt fixtures and two 575-watt balltracker fixtures. The entire system will have a total of one hundred seventy-five 1410-watt fixtures  twenty-five 1170-watt fixtures  and twenty 575-watt balltracker fixtures.nThe proposed lighting system upgrade will not pose any issues with air traffic flying over the field. The original lighting system was certified as such by Raleigh-Durham International Airport (RDU) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). All new poles and fixtures will match the existing lighting heights.nAll designs will be certified by structural engineers. These will also be reviewed and inspected by the Town of Morrisville Building Inspections department in compliance with all applicable building regulations including electrical design  wind loads  and ice loads.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The site address is 5800 Cricket Pitch Way and is near the intersection of Church Street and McCrimmon Parkway in Morrisville  NC.  The location is a recreational field in a public park called Church Street Park that is situated in a "mixed use" residential and commercial area.  The site is located approximately 16 235 feet southwest of the RDU International Airport runway 5L threshold and beneath the Precision instrument Runway Approach Zone.
